%%PASS=1%%
<script>
	// inline block comment — parens preserved for comment
	const a = () => x /* c */;

	// curried arrow — outer parens preserved for comment
	const b = (a) => (b) => z /* c */;

	// multiple levels — each level preserves parens
	const c = (a) => (b) => (c) => w /* c1 */ /* c2 */;

	// line comment — forces multiline parens
	const d = () =>
		x; // c

	// own-line block comment — forces multiline parens
	const e = () =>
		x;
		/* c */

	// stacked line comments — each kept on its own line (no swallow)
	const g = () =>
		x; // c1
		// c2

	// leading + trailing — leading hugs `=>`, trailing keeps parens
	const h = () => /* lead */ x /* trail */;

	// ternary body, leading + trailing — the retained parens keep the leading comment outside
	const k = () => (/* lead */ cond ? a : b /* trail */);

	// leading line comment — the run drops to its own line, the retained parens below it
	const l = () =>
		// lead
		x /* trail */;

	// leading block then line — the run stays together above the body
	const m = () =>
		/* lead1 */ // lead2
		x /* trail */;

	// same-line comment group after a body break — block + line stay together
	const i = () =>
		x;
		/* i1 */ // i2

	// sequence body — the pair the sequence prints for ITSELF stands in for the erased
	// shell, so the comment stays on the last operand inside it from every authoring
	const n = () => (
		x,
		y
		// t
	);

	// the block spelling of the same, collapsed inline in that pair
	const o = () => (
		x,
		y
		/* t */
	);

	// object-literal body — parens are required, comment kept inside (not after `)`)
	const j = () => ({ k: 1 }) /* c */;

	// inside call arg — parens preserved
	f(() => x /* c */);
</script>
